quote: Theorem 3 (Li and Li, 2016). Suppose X_{λ1}, . . . , X_{λn} is a set of independent non-negative random variables where X_{λi} has survival function F̄(·; λi), i = 1, . . . , n with λi > 0. Also suppose Ip1, . . . , Ipn are independent Bernoulli random variables with E(Ipi) = pi, independent of the X_{λi}. Suppose (a) F̄(·; λi) is increasing and concave in λi; (b) Σ_{i=1}^n X_{λi} is Schur-concave in the λi's. Then (λ1, . . . , λn) ≽^m (μ1, . . . , μn) ⇒ Σ_{i=1}^n I_{p_{i:n}} X_{μ_{n−i+1:n}} ≥st Σ_{i=1}^n I_{p_{i:n}} X_{λ_{n−i+1:n}}.

quote: Theorem 4. Suppose X_{λ1}, . . . , X_{λn} is a set of independent non-negative random variables where X_{λi} has survival function F̄(·; λi), i = 1, . . . , n with λi > 0. Also suppose Ip1, . . . , Ipn are independent Bernoulli random variables with E(Ipi) = pi, independent of the X_{λi}. Suppose (a) F̄(·; λi) is increasing and concave in λi; (b) Σ_{i=1}^n X_{λi} is Schur-concave in the λi's. If (λ, −h(p)) ∈ Un and (μ, −h(q)) ∈ Un, where Un = {(a, b) = (a1 . . . an ; b1 . . . bn) : ai > 0, bi < 0, (ai − aj)(bi − bj) ≥ 0}, then (matrix) (λ1 . . . λn ; −h(p1) . . . −h(pn)) >> (μ1 . . . μn ; −h(q1) . . . −h(qn)) implies Σ_{i=1}^n I_{qi} X_{μi} ≥st Σ_{i=1}^n I_{pi} X_{λi}, where h(p) = −log p or h(p) = (1 − p)/p.
